messages.subject: about paramter contrain
parts:
Dear stan experts,
    In my model, one parameter (i.e., kappa) is at the denominator, which cannot be (but needs to be above) 0. It also has a upper bound, namely 1.
    I've used the phi_approx function, namely kappa[i] = Phi_approx(x); (x is a real number) however, it turns out to be that kappa could still be 0.
    Now I change it to inv_logit, namely kappa[i] = inv_logit (x). But I don't know whether it works. 
    I am wondering whether you have some idea on that. Thanks for your help and have a nice weekend!

Best,
Yang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] about paramter contrain
parts:
If you want kappa in (0, 1) declare it as:

real<lower=0, upper=1> kappa;

You can also define

real kappa_raw;

real<lower=0, upper=1> kappa = inv_logit(kappa_raw);

But if you do the latter, then you have to put the prior on kappa_raw
or adjust for the Jacobian of the transform yourself.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] about paramter contrain
parts:
It may be underflowing to zero. inv_logit() is going to underflow
around -400 or so, I think, and Phi() is probably in the same orde
of magnitude. So you might want to look at the inputs to Phi() that
are causing it to underflow and figuring out how to control those.
In many cases, a weakly informative prior can solve a lot of these problems.

- Bob
